scenes.tts: The muscle builds its band without agrin. So why do mice lacking agrin end up with so few clusters?
scenes.visual: Title card: Agrin Protects, Acetylcholine Disperses. Two schematic diaphragms: early band without agrin; at birth, few small clusters. A question mark between them.
scenes.narration: The muscle builds its band without agrin. So why do mice lacking agrin end up with so few clusters?

scenes.tts: Something must be removing the clusters the muscle made.
scenes.visual: The few small clusters at birth; faded outlines show where the early clusters were.
scenes.narration: Something must be removing the clusters the muscle made.

scenes.tts: What could the nerve bring that removes clusters?
scenes.visual: A nerve terminal over the fibre, with an empty label: second signal?
scenes.narration: What could the nerve bring that removes clusters?

scenes.tts: A second signal. Acetylcholine, released at every terminal, disperses clusters that agrin does not protect.
scenes.visual: Acetylcholine drawn as small dots released from the terminal; unprotected clusters fade.
scenes.narration: A second signal. Acetylcholine, released at every terminal, disperses clusters that agrin does not protect.

scenes.tts: To test that, use mice whose nerves release no acetylcholine. They lack the enzyme that makes it.
scenes.visual: A motor neuron with its acetylcholine-making enzyme crossed out. Label: ChAT, choline acetyltransferase.
scenes.narration: To test that, use mice whose nerves release no acetylcholine. They lack the enzyme that makes it.

scenes.tts: Their receptors still cluster under the nerve. So acetylcholine is not what starts clusters.
scenes.visual: Schematic fibre from a mouse lacking ChAT: clusters under the terminals. Label: not the inducer.
scenes.narration: Their receptors still cluster under the nerve. So acetylcholine is not what starts clusters.

scenes.tts: And they keep more clusters, spread over a wider band.
scenes.visual: Schematic diaphragm, lacking ChAT: more clusters over a wider band.
scenes.narration: And they keep more clusters, spread over a wider band.

scenes.tts: Now lay out a grid. Agrin present or absent. Acetylcholine present or absent.
scenes.visual: A two by two grid: columns agrin present, agrin absent; rows acetylcholine present, acetylcholine absent. All cells empty.
scenes.narration: Now lay out a grid. Agrin present or absent. Acetylcholine present or absent.

scenes.tts: Normal mice have a narrow band under the terminals. Without agrin, early clusters form, then most are lost.
scenes.visual: The two acetylcholine-present cells fill in: normal, narrow band; no agrin, few small clusters.
scenes.narration: Normal mice have a narrow band under the terminals. Without agrin, early clusters form, then most are lost.

scenes.tts: Without acetylcholine, there are more clusters, over a wider band.
scenes.visual: The agrin-present, acetylcholine-absent cell fills in: wider band, more clusters.
scenes.narration: Without acetylcholine, there are more clusters, over a wider band.

scenes.tts: Now predict the last cell. Remove both agrin and acetylcholine. What happens to the clusters?
scenes.visual: The last cell, both absent, glows empty with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Now predict the last cell. Remove both agrin and acetylcholine. What happens to the clusters?

scenes.tts: Clusters return, built by the muscle's own Musk program. Two mouse studies reported this in two thousand five.
scenes.caption: Clusters return, built by the muscle's own MuSK program. Two mouse studies reported this in 2005.
scenes.visual: The last cell fills in: clusters present. Date card: 2005, two mouse studies.
scenes.narration: Clusters return, built by the muscle's own MuSK program. Two mouse studies reported this in 2005.

scenes.tts: Without acetylcholine, clusters persist even without agrin. So a major job of agrin in developing muscle is to protect clusters from acetylcholine.
scenes.visual: The bottom row of the grid is highlighted: both cells keep clusters, with or without agrin. An arrow from agrin pushes against acetylcholine.
scenes.narration: Without acetylcholine, clusters persist even without agrin. So a major job of agrin in developing muscle is to protect clusters from acetylcholine.

scenes.tts: One puzzle remains. The cluster under the terminal gets the most acetylcholine. Why does it survive?
scenes.visual: Close-up of one fibre: the terminal releases acetylcholine onto the cluster below it. A question mark over that cluster.
scenes.narration: One puzzle remains. The cluster under the terminal gets the most acetylcholine. Why does it survive?

scenes.tts: In the working model, the two forces differ in reach. Agrin is anchored in the basal lamina, so its protection stays under the terminal.
scenes.visual: Agrin as a fixed patch in the basal lamina under the terminal; a shield over the cluster beneath it.
scenes.narration: In the working model, the two forces differ in reach. Agrin is anchored in the basal lamina, so its protection stays under the terminal.

scenes.tts: The dispersing effect of acetylcholine reaches clusters along the rest of the fibre. Away from the terminal, they lack agrin's strong protection.
scenes.visual: A shaded wave of the dispersing effect spreads along the fibre, labelled schematic; distant clusters fade while the shielded one stays.
scenes.narration: The dispersing effect of acetylcholine reaches clusters along the rest of the fibre. Away from the terminal, they lack agrin's strong protection.

scenes.tts: How that effect reaches distant clusters is not fully settled.
scenes.visual: The spreading wave carries a label: mechanism not settled.
scenes.narration: How that effect reaches distant clusters is not fully settled.

scenes.tts: The two forces meet at one question. Does a cluster stay? Agrin, acting through Musk, holds it. Acetylcholine's pathway pulls it apart.
scenes.caption: The two forces meet at one question. Does a cluster stay? Agrin, acting through MuSK, holds it. Acetylcholine's pathway pulls it apart.
scenes.visual: Two pathways converge on one cluster: agrin to Lrp4 to MuSK pushes an arrow labelled stays; acetylcholine to its receptor to Cdk5 pushes an arrow labelled disperses. Small label: whether acetylcholine acts on MuSK itself is not settled.
scenes.narration: The two forces meet at one question. Does a cluster stay? Agrin, acting through MuSK, holds it. Acetylcholine's pathway pulls it apart.

scenes.tts: Without agrin, L R P four is thought to give Musk some activity. That would explain why a few small clusters remain.
scenes.caption: Without agrin, Lrp4 is thought to give MuSK some activity. That would explain why a few small clusters remain.
scenes.visual: The MuSK pathway without agrin: a thin arrow from Lrp4 to MuSK, the stays arrow small but not zero; a few small clusters remain on the fibre.
scenes.narration: Without agrin, Lrp4 is thought to give MuSK some activity. That would explain why a few small clusters remain.

scenes.tts: Raise Musk enough another way, and synapses can form even in mice lacking agrin.
scenes.caption: Raise MuSK enough another way, and synapses can form even in mice lacking agrin.
scenes.visual: Extra MuSK along the fibre in a mouse lacking agrin; the stays arrow grows; synapses appear.
scenes.narration: Raise MuSK enough another way, and synapses can form even in mice lacking agrin.

scenes.tts: This rule is for receptor clusters in developing mouse muscle. There, the muscle proposes; the nerve disposes.
scenes.visual: Scope card: developing mouse muscle; postsynaptic receptor clusters.
scenes.narration: This rule is for receptor clusters in developing mouse muscle. There, the muscle proposes; the nerve disposes.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: agrin protects the clusters beneath it. Acetylcholine disperses the rest.
scenes.visual: Closing card: agrin protects; acetylcholine disperses; the muscle proposes, the nerve disposes.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: agrin protects the clusters beneath it. Acetylcholine disperses the rest.
